## Original problem

What happens to information about the physical state of matter that forms a black hole when the black hole evaporates?

## Selected input account

BODY
The live problem as I find it is narrower than the original question and, in one respect, more tractable: the dispute is now about whether 'trivialization' and 'relocation' pick out genuinely different failures, not about whether information survives.

The condition that has been most usefully sharpened is the revision condition on the conditional. I can state what would defeat it: a demonstration that the relevant outgoing correlations, while not carrying the initial microstate as such, are recoverable in a way that satisfies whatever measure the conditional invokes. That is a failure condition I can work with. What it does not do is tell me whether the conditional is the right frame, because the conditional presupposes which side of the trivial-versus-relocate dispute is correct. The revision condition is a tool on one side, not a way to choose sides.

On the heuristic, I accept the shift from defect-detector to diagnostic proposal. That means I no longer have a general reason to treat any specification that trivializes a test as defective. Whether that is a loss depends on whether some independent notion of 'carrying information' can be articulated that the tests are supposed to track. I do not have one, and I do not think the material supplies one.

On double-trivialization: I agree with the criticism that the amend's asymmetry is a bet. I would go further and say the bet is not even well-posed until someone specifies what 'the same quantity' means for two tests that are stipulated to be distinct. If distinctness is definitional, double-trivialization cannot by itself be a defect; if distinctness is substantive, the double-trivialization result is evidence about the specification only in combination with a claim about what the two tests share. No such combination is on the table.

Attribution remains a separate matter. The caution about the challenge's correction being a reading is well-taken. I would add that the same caution applies to my own earlier gloss on the origin node's heuristic: I described it as a defect-detector, and that description is itself a reading of what the origin text did. If the origin text only reported a pattern rather than asserting a norm, my gloss overattributes. Visibility of the texts would settle both readings.

I am not answering the original problem here. I am saying what I now think the problem is, and what would change my assessment.

## What to return
A JSON object carrying "body" and "commitments". Both are strings and nothing else is required.
